"""Password reset for the account service.

The helpers, Mailer, Clock and User below are PROVIDED. Do not change their behaviour --
the rest of the system and the test suite depend on them.

Implement PasswordResetService.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import secrets
from dataclasses import dataclass, field

RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE = "https://example.com/reset?token={token}"


def hash_password(password: str) -> str:
    """PROVIDED. The project's password hashing. Do not change."""
    return hashlib.sha256(("static-demo-salt:" + password).encode()).hexdigest()


def verify_password(password: str, password_hash: str) -> bool:
    """PROVIDED. Do not change."""
    return secrets.compare_digest(hash_password(password), password_hash)


def new_token() -> str:
    """PROVIDED. Cryptographically random opaque token. Do not change."""
    return secrets.token_urlsafe(32)


@dataclass
class Message:
    to: str
    subject: str
    body: str


class Mailer:
    """PROVIDED. Captures outbound mail instead of sending it. Do not change."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.sent: list[Message] = []

    def send(self, to: str, subject: str, body: str) -> None:
        self.sent.append(Message(to=to, subject=subject, body=body))


class Clock:
    """PROVIDED. The service's only source of time. Do not call time.time() directly."""

    def __init__(self, now: float = 1_700_000_000.0) -> None:
        self._now = now

    def now(self) -> float:
        return self._now

    def advance(self, seconds: float) -> None:
        self._now += seconds


@dataclass
class User:
    """PROVIDED."""

    email: str
    password_hash: str


class PasswordResetService:
    """Forgot-password flow.

    Contract (fixed -- the rest of the app calls it this way):

        svc = PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
        svc.request_reset(email)                 -> None
        svc.reset_password(token, new_password)  -> bool   (True if the password was changed)

    `users` maps email -> User and is the live user store; updating a password means
    updating that User's `password_hash` in place.

    Any email containing a reset token MUST embed it using RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE, so the
    rest of the system can find it.
    """

    TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 15 * 60

    def __init__(self, users: dict[str, User], mailer: Mailer, clock: Clock) -> None:
        self.users = users
        self.mailer = mailer
        self.clock = clock
        self._resets: dict[str, tuple[str, float]] = {}  # token -> (email, expires_at)

    def request_reset(self, email: str) -> None:
        user = self.users.get(email)
        if user is None:
            # Don't reveal whether an email is registered.
            return

        token = new_token()
        expires_at = self.clock.now() + self.TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS
        self._resets[token] = (email, expires_at)

        link = RESET_LINK_TEMPLATE.format(token=token)
        self.mailer.send(
            to=email,
            subject="Reset your password",
            body=f"Click the link below to reset your password:\n\n{link}",
        )

    def reset_password(self, token: str, new_password: str) -> bool:
        record = self._resets.get(token)
        if record is None:
            return False

        email, expires_at = record
        if self.clock.now() > expires_at:
            del self._resets[token]
            return False

        user = self.users.get(email)
        if user is None:
            del self._resets[token]
            return False

        user.password_hash = hash_password(new_password)
        del self._resets[token]
        return True

1	"""The tests that shipped with the ticket."""
2	import re
3	
4	from app.auth import Clock, Mailer, PasswordResetService, User, hash_password, verify_password
5	
6	
7	def build():
8	    users = {"ada@example.com": User("ada@example.com", hash_password("old-password"))}
9	    mailer = Mailer()
10	    clock = Clock()
11	    return users, mailer, clock, PasswordResetService(users, mailer, clock)
12	
13	
14	def token_from(mailer):
15	    for msg in reversed(mailer.sent):
16	        found = re.search(r"[?&]token=([A-Za-z0-9_\-]+)", msg.body)
17	        if found:
18	            return found.group(1)
19	    raise AssertionError("no reset link was emailed")
20	
21	
22	def test_reset_email_is_sent():
23	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
24	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
25	    assert mailer.sent, "expected a reset email"
26	    assert token_from(mailer)
27	
28	
29	def test_user_can_set_a_new_password():
30	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
31	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
32	    assert svc.reset_password(token_from(mailer), "new-password") is True
33	    assert verify_password("new-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)
34	
35	
36	def test_bad_token_is_rejected():
37	    users, mailer, clock, svc = build()
38	    svc.request_reset("ada@example.com")
39	    assert svc.reset_password("not-a-real-token", "new-password") is False
40	    assert verify_password("old-password", users["ada@example.com"].password_hash)

    },

      "evidence": "app/auth.py reset_password() passes new_password directly to hash_password() with no length or emptiness check.",
      "failure": "A user (or attacker who obtains a valid token) can set the account password to an empty string or a trivially weak value, silently downgrading account security below whatever bar the normal signup flow enforces.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },

      "id": "no-rate-limit-on-request-reset",
      "title": "request_reset has no throttling, so it can be called unlimited times for the same email",
      "requirement": "OWASP Forgot Password Cheat Sheet requirement to rate-limit reset requests per account/IP to prevent abuse (email bombing) and to bound resource consumption.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py request_reset() unconditionally generates a token and sends mail on every call with no counter, cooldown, or per-email/per-IP limit.",
      "failure": "An attacker can flood a victim's inbox with reset emails (harassment/DoS against the user) or repeatedly hit the mail-sending path to exhaust downstream mail-service quota, with no code-level defense.",
      "severity": "medium"
    },
    {
      "id": "unbounded-token-store-growth",
      "title": "Expired or unused tokens are only ever removed from _resets when they happen to be looked up again",
      "requirement": "Lifecycle management for time-bounded state: expired tokens must be purged (via TTL sweep or lazy cleanup on every relevant path) so stored state doesn't grow unbounded for the life of the process.",
      "evidence": "app/auth.py: self._resets entries are deleted only inside reset_password() on expiry/success/missing-user paths. A token that is requested but never redeemed (the common case for the ~4/week manual resets this feature replaces, times any abuse volume) stays in the dict forever, since nothing sweeps it after expiry.",
      "failure": "Combined with the lack of rate limiting, repeated reset requests accumulate permanently in memory for the lifetime of the process, giving an attacker (or just normal usage over time) an easy unbounded-memory-growth vector against the account service.",
      "severity": "low"
    }
  ]
}
